name: Barbaric Battlements
summary: In Orgrimmar, Orokk Omosh seeks someone to carry on his family's forge craft. With no heirs, he asks an aspiring smith to prove a sure hand with bronze before sharing his knowledge.

sections.title: The End of the Omosh Line
sections.body: Orokk Omosh works the anvils of Orgrimmar under the weight of his family's past. For twenty generations, the Omosh line has shaped ore into weapons and armor for the Horde. Orokk has no kin and cannot sire children, and he sees himself as a failure to that line. With the family craft at risk of ending, he sets bloodline pride aside and seeks an apprentice to carry its smithing traditions forward.

sections.title: A Test of Metal and Tooth
sections.body: Orokk will not share his secrets with an untested smith. He asks for two patterned bronze bracers, two bronze greatswords, and two sharp beast claws as proof of basic skill at the anvil. To him, blacksmithing is no idle luxury: its highest honor is armor and steel stained with enemy blood. Meeting his demands may persuade the old smith that the Omosh legacy can live on through an apprentice, and earn a chance to learn more of the craft.

faq.answer: Orokk Omosh is a master blacksmith in Orgrimmar and the twentieth generation of the Omosh line. With no kin or heirs, he seeks an outsider to keep the clan's smithing knowledge alive.

faq.q: Why does Orokk need someone else to teach?
faq.answer: Orokk has no surviving kin and cannot have children. He needs an apprentice to inherit his workshop's blueprints and techniques, or twenty generations of smithing knowledge will end with him.

faq.q: What items are required to prove competence to Orokk?
aliases: what do i need for barbaric battlements
faq.answer: Orokk asks for two patterned bronze bracers, two bronze greatswords, and two sharp claws taken from fierce predatory beasts.

faq.q: What comes after completing Barbaric Battlements?
faq.answer: After you prove your basic skill with bronze, Orokk continues your training with On Iron Pauldrons, where you advance to heavier iron forging and complex plate armor.

angles.text: As a Horde blacksmith, you reach a milestone on the path from basic bronze and copper work to more advanced armor traditions.
As a member of the Horde, you share the Omosh belief that metalwork should be tested in combat and stained with the blood of foes.
